All 22 carry C overlap; 18 are structurally pure viewpoint drift (A+C) where the nearest preceding name is the CORRECT male name, usually Hugo in the previous sentence.

Most Hugo-as-she drifts are cataphoric: sentence-initial 'She' followed by a female name later in the same sentence as OBJECT ('She caught Dr. Finch's eye', 'She turned to Dr. Finch', 'She glanced at Dr. Finch', 'She remembered... Eleanor's watch'). A detector using nearest-preceding-antecedent gender will mark these sentences consistent and miss them; the giveaway signature is [She + investigator-action-verb + female-name-as-object].

Drift is sticky in runs of 2 consecutive sentences: once narration drifts, the next sentence stays in the wrong gender (ch1 'She moved closer'->'past her', ch1 'She felt the weight'->'fell to her', ch6 'she knew'->'she sensed', ch10 'She felt the ache'->'she sensed'). 8 of 27 instances are continuations of an immediately preceding drifted sentence.

All are class B adjacent-antecedent binds (the pronoun takes the gender of the other character in the sentence). A fix targeting only Hugo-as-she leaves these.
